scope: Corollary 6.1 (Finite-dimensional ℓp bounds) of the manuscript “The Euclidean Steinitz–Bergström theorem” (preprints/The-Euclidean-Steinitz-Bergstrom-theorem-September-24-2026/The-Euclidean-Steinitz-Bergstrom-theorem-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 097 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d8924ac01b6d4dc0), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 26. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞, with 1/∞ = 0, and let d, N ≥ 1 be integers. Every sequence v1, . . . , vN ∈ Rd with ∥vi∥p ≤ 1 admits signs εi ∈ {−1, 1} such that max 0≤k≤N ‖ ‖ ‖ ‖ ‖ k ∑ i=1 εivi ‖ ‖ ‖ ‖ ‖ p ≤ Cdmax{1/p, 1−1/p} . If additionally ∑N i=1 vi = 0, there is a permutation π ∈ SN such that max 0≤k≤N ‖ ‖ ‖ ‖ ‖ k ∑ i=1 vπ(i) ‖ ‖ ‖ ‖ ‖ p ≤ Cdmax{1/p, 1−1/p} . Here C is the same absolute constant as in Theorems 1.1 and 1.2, independent of p, d, N. For 1 ≤ p ≤ 2, both bounds have sharp dimension order d1/p: for every d there is a unit-ball sequence for which every signing has a prefix of norm at least d1/p, and a finite indexed zero-sum unit-ball family for which every permutation has a prefix of norm at least 1 3d1/p.
